q: people have been telling me to incorporate more red meat into my diet to help with the anemia but I had my gallbladder removed last month
cx: Advice she keeps getting that doesn't fit her history.

q: I have attended all my appointments, she just didn’t mention it as they don’t raise cause for concern until it’s 105. I just feel betrayed
cx: At 35 weeks she learned of a months-old blood result by accident.

q: I guess I wasn’t prepared for the fact that my newborn would not be sleeping at all at night. And I mean at all.
cx: Five days after her first birth, three nights home.

q: Yes we’re currently doing shifts
cx: Night shifts with her partner in the first week.

q: It’s been a rough pregnancy (after two that I realize now were relatively easy) and I don’t know how I’m going to survive the rest.
cx: 35 weeks in a third pregnancy.

q: I have 2 more weeks until maternity leave starts, 2 other kids under 3, and an exhausted husband who is handling me on top of them some days.
cx: Counting down to leave with two under three.

q: I’m just so over having to take care of myself on top of taking care of the baby. My own recovery has taken so much mental energy since birth
cx: Weeks after birth, one recovery problem after another.

q: Our turnover rate is very high because she fires people left and right which scares me.
cx: 11 weeks, two months into a new job, deciding whether to tell her boss.

q: My manager advised that I wait to tell my boss, but I feel guilty lying and have to request time off of work for appointments and such.
cx: Appointments force the question of telling work.

q: Unfortunately I work for a small business, so my boss is the owner- therefore SHE is the HR department.
cx: Nobody to go to at work but the boss.

q: I just don’t want to lose a job while pregnant since it’s so hard to find a job while being pregnant.
cx: Why she plans a paper trail.

q: So of course I’m doing the “tips and tricks” to help with priming for labor - dates*, raspberry leaf tea, the Starbucks passion tea when I go there, LOTS of walking and movement, labor exercises from YouTube.
cx: 38 weeks with her first, listing what she is trying.

q: the entire intent was equipment/process familiarization as well as maybe a small backup amount. As a FTM I had very low expectations for what I would produce
cx: Why she started collecting colostrum before the birth.

q: I have struggled with body image and weight issues my entire life and I really don’t want to gain a lot of weight.
cx: Just found out, first baby.

q: Can someone please provide me with some insight on what to expect? I read some posts by bigger girls that they only gained 15-20 lb when pregnant.
cx: Looking for experiences from women her size.

q: the only way I can describe it that feeling when you wait in a rollercoaster line forever, and when you finally make it to the end you want to chicken out and turn back but it’s too late.
cx: The night before an induction at 41+1.

q: I really need support and something good to fill my head with because my mom keeps telling me induction is bad.
cx: Why she asks for positive induction stories.

q: i catch myself losing my patience with my other kids & spouse. This week we had a major change in the house and my brother, his wife & 1 yo, had to move in as an emergency.
cx: Pregnant with older children and relatives suddenly living with them.

q: by the end of the night im upset & all i want is to get away from everyone.
cx: Evenings in a full house.

q: I was so anxious during the whole first trimester with my first and I am on the verge of panicking with this ultra early positive.
cx: A surprise positive at 3w2d after years of trying.

q: That was my major anxiety with my first pregnancy as well! Once I could feel him I felt so much better
cx: What eased the worry last time.
